title: fix(core): honour `measure.format` on the datetime arm of a date-shaped measure
body:
Fixes #8352

A dataset measure over a `datetime` field now honours `measure.format`, the way one over a `date` field already did.

## The defect

`formatMeasureDate` routes a date-shaped measure down one of two arms. The date arm threaded `format` onward; the datetime arm called `formatDateTime(v, { locale })` and dropped it:

```
dataset-format.ts:192   formatDate(v, format, { locale });   ← format IS threaded in
dataset-format.ts:195   formatDateTime(v, { locale });       ← format is DROPPED
```

That is structural, not a threading slip: `formatDateTime(value, options?)` has **no style parameter**, so the datetime arm could not honour `format` even in principle. A `Field.date` yields `2026-09-08` and takes the first arm; a `Field.datetime` yields `2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z` and takes the second.

## The fix, and the two shapes it deliberately is not

The datetime arm **selects** a formatter instead of threading one. No published signature moved.

**Not** a new parameter on `formatDateTime`. That is a published signature, and its own docblock already records why the positional shape was refused there.

**Not** the one-line pass-through `formatDateTime(v, { locale, style: format })`. This looks like the obvious fix and is the defect inverted — measured before the real fix was written:

| input `format` | date arm today | pass-through would give | shipped fix gives |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `'relative'` | `In 2 days` | `Sep 11, 2026, 09:30 AM` (ignored) | `In 2 days` |
| `'short'` | `Sep 11, '26` | `Sep 11, 2026, 09:30 AM` (ignored) | `9/11/2026 9:30 am` |
| `'compact'` | `Sep 11` (not honoured) | `9/11/2026 9:30 am` (honoured!) | `Sep 11, 2026, 09:30 AM` |

`options.style`'s vocabulary is `'compact'` alone, so the pass-through honours the one word the date arm does **not** honour while still ignoring both words it does. A test pins that this path does not do it.

## Which styles, per arm — enumerated before deciding, not assumed

Measured on `formatDate`, which is what the date arm actually calls: `'short'` and `'relative'` change the output; `'compact'`, `'YYYY-MM-DD'`, `''` and absent all fall to the default locale face. So the honoured set is exactly two words, and the datetime arm's honoured set is now **equal** to it — no more, no less, asserted as a computed set over both arms rather than claimed.

Which **face** each word selects is per-arm, because the arms render different types:

- `'relative'` resolves through `formatRelativeDate` on **both** arms — the same function, so the same calendar day reads the same phrase for either field type. Its ±7-day fallback is **inherited, not re-decided here**: putting a second copy of that window in this file is objectui#4576 exactly, which this repo has already paid for once.
- `'short'` resolves to the dense narrow-card face of the value's own type: `formatDate`'s `'short'` for a date, `formatDateTime`'s `'compact'` for a datetime. The datetime face keeps the time of day, and is byte-identical to what a `datetime` grid cell already paints — so a measure tile and a cell showing the same instant cannot drift.

**Declared consequence:** an out-of-window datetime with `format: 'relative'` renders the absolute **date** face (`Oct 19`), not the absolute datetime face. That is `formatRelativeDate`'s own fallback and is identical to what the date arm does. `'relative'` is day-granular by construction — it shows no time inside the window either — so showing one only outside it would be the inconsistent option.

## The docblocks, qualified by arm

The wording above `formatMeasure` said `format: 'short'` and `format: 'relative'` **are honoured**, full stop. True of the date arm, false of the datetime arm — and an objectstack triage pass read it, concluded the defect was fixed, and downgraded the card, which a driven browser run then refuted. Both docblocks now state the date arm and the datetime arm separately. The arms agree today, but the undifferentiated sentence is not coming back: it is what hid the disagreement, and it would read as true now for a reason that has nothing to do with why it was written.

## Tests — the three-leg pin, and why it is shaped this way

`formatRelativeDate` falls back to the absolute form beyond ±7 days, so **an out-of-window value renders identically whether `format` is honoured or dropped**. Both readings that missed this defect were taken that way (`2026-07-04` and `2026-07-28`, 40–60 days old). The suite's existing `format` cases use 2024 values *and never pass a datetime through them at all* — that pair is why this was invisible to it.

The new cases pin the clock (`vi.setSystemTime`, the convention already in `plugin-timeline` / `plugin-map`; the suite pins `TZ=UTC`) and measure in-window and out-of-window separately.

Directions **measured** by ablating the shipped fix four ways — A = the pre-fix arm; B1 = wire the arm to `formatRelativeDate` unconditionally; B2 = hand-roll the relative phrase, skipping the window; C = the pass-through above:

| case | A | B1 | B2 | C |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| leg 1 · in-window datetime is relative | RED | RED | RED | RED |
| leg 2 · date-only positive control | green | green | green | green |
| leg 3 · out-of-window datetime is absolute | RED | green | RED | RED |
| the decisive pair (both arms agree) | RED | green | RED | RED |
| `short` parity | RED | RED | green | RED |
| vocabulary equality | RED | RED | green | RED |
| pass-through anti-pin | green | green | green | RED |
| unstyled-default guard | green | RED | green | green |

Leg 2 is the **rig check** and stays green under every ablation of the datetime arm — that is what makes it a control. It first carried the cross-arm assertion too and went red under A; that was corrected and the pair is its own case, because a control that the defect can move is not one.

Each fake fix leaves something green: B1 leaves leg 3 and the pair green, B2 leaves `short` and vocabulary green. The two must-not-move guards separate them — B1 is the only column reddening the unstyled-default guard, C the only one reddening the pass-through anti-pin.

⚠️ One prediction was wrong and is recorded as corrected rather than restated: leg 3 was predicted green-on-both-sides and measured **RED** under A, because out of the window the honoured reading renders the absolute date face while the pre-fix arm rendered the absolute datetime face.

Every ablation leg mutated the file on disk, proved the mutation landed (blob hash moved, marker counted), ran, then restored via `git checkout HEAD -- path` and proved the restore by blob hash equality plus an empty `git diff HEAD`.

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core test` — **134 files, 2855 tests, 0 failed**
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core type-check` — exit 0 (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`); the new test file confirmed present in the checked set via `--listFiles`, not assumed
- Dependency closure built first (`pnpm --filter "@object-ui/core^..." build`) — the first type-check run failed `TS6305` on an unbuilt `packages/types/dist`, i.e. a stale-artifact false red
- Gates, each by its own verdict line, all exit 0: `check:control-bytes` (7042 files scanned), `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:self-import`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:comment-mask-corpus` (report-only, pre-existing residue at its held ceiling, unmoved), `check:governed-queue-guard`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`
- Governed-surface guard run with `AGENTS.md` as the **lit control**: control reports GOVERNED, this PR's three paths report NOT GOVERNED
- Repo-wide `pnpm lint` / full `pnpm test` are CI's run, not claimed here
- Measured at commit `f4fdbbb44`

## 验收备注

**Not measured, not resolved.** Whether any *published* app hits this today — the card marks it NOT MEASURED and nothing here changes that.

**Untouched, deliberately:**
- objectui#8263's subject (the `Date.parse` impossible-date guard on this same function) — sequenced behind this card, and independently confirmed still `pm:queue` and unassigned, so the card's serial constraint naming it as in-flight is stale.
- `formatDateTime`'s `'—'` return for empty/invalid values — objectui#8507's family, awaiting its own ruling.
- The server half — the card records it as already corrected and confirmed live; see objectstack#16101 and objectstack#16238.

**Noted, not filed** (no PR or person is on track to touch these):
- The pre-existing `honours relative` case for the date arm uses a 2024 value, so it is an agreement assertion that cannot distinguish the relative face from the absolute one. Now covered by the in-window legs beside it; left as-is rather than widening this diff.
- `formatRelativeDate` still does not read `options.style`; the interface doc already records that as a deliberate open question, so it is not a new observation.

**Filed separately:** the same class of defect one surface over — `DateTimeCellRenderer` passes `field.format` straight into `options.style`, so a `datetime` grid column silently drops `format: 'relative'` while a `date` column honours it. Out of scope here (different package, different surface, new verification surface), so it is a card rather than a rider. Issue link in the report.
